symptom: A backslash in a flow expression's string was stored wrong: under `mdl 1;` `declare $s String = 'C:\temp\new'` stored `'C:\\temp\\new'` (describe under the header printed it doubled); without the header `'C:\\temp'` also stored two backslashes, and an expression stored as written (spanning lines, or an unspaced operator) holding `'it\'s'` stored `'it\'s'` — CE0117 in mx check — while `fmt --upgrade --header` of it produced mdl 1 that did not parse. The quote scanner ended the literal at `\'`, so `'it\'s'+'x'` was rendered instead of stored as written.
cause: The mdl 0 escape rule leaked into the model from two sides. mendixexpr.QuoteLiteral re-doubled a backslash before n/r/t/\/' so that describe's verbatim output would re-read under mdl 0 — putting the MDL escape into the stored expression, under mdl 1 too, where nothing decodes it. And an expression stored as written kept the mdl 0 spelling of its literals, whose AST value was the unescaped one; shouldPreserveExpressionSource scanned strings with '' as the only escape whatever the language.
fix: QuoteLiteral writes the Mendix spelling of the value (apostrophe doubled, nothing else). Under mdl 0 an expression stored as written has each literal holding a backslash rewritten to the Mendix spelling of its unescaped value (storedExpressionSource, also for template-param / trailing-whitespace SourceExprs and send-rest-request params); the scanner takes the lexing rule (stringLiteralEnd). describeExpr(ctx, …) writes a stored backslash in a flow expression's string as `\\` under mdl 0. escapeFix requotes the literals of an expression stored as written. Workflow and widget expressions stay stored as written in both languages (bareArgumentText no longer goes through buildSourceExpression).
insight: Store the value; spell it for the reader at describe time. A store that pre-escapes for the describe→exec round trip keeps the round trip green while writing the wrong bytes — the #810 doubling was stable in every describe test and only visible by reading the stored expression, which is what the table test in mdl/roundtrip/expression_string_escape_test.go does (language x literal x the three storage paths: rendered, spanning lines, unspaced operator). Evidence: mx check on a TestApp copy rejects the old build's `'it\'s'` expression with CE0117 and accepts `'C:\'+'x'`, so Mendix has no backslash escape.
